identification.name: Stainless Steel 316 (Annealed)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely stocked in sheet, plate, tube, and bar. 316L (low-carbon variant) preferred for welded assemblies to prevent sensitisation; for metal-AM-printed parts, see the dedicated Stainless Steel 316L (DMLS) entry in this database rather than this wrought/annealed entry.
identification.notes: Austenitic stainless steel with 2–3% Mo addition for superior chloride and pitting corrosion resistance compared to 304/303. Yield strength (200 MPa) is the EN (European Norm) 10088-3 minimum for annealed bar; ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials) A276 specifies a minimum of 207 MPa (30 ksi). Tensile strength 517 MPa is the ASTM A276 minimum of 75 ksi converted to metric. 316L (low carbon, ≤0.03% C) is preferred when welding and is the standard grade used for metal AM (additive manufacturing) (DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering)/SLM (Selective Laser Melting) and Binder Jet); the lower carbon content prevents sensitisation during the thermal cycles of AM and welding. Electrical conductivity derived from resistivity of 0.74 µΩ·m. Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3 = 517/1.732 ≈ 299 MPa. Melting point is solidus (1375°C); liquidus 1400°C (MatWeb).

typical_usage: Marine hardware, boat fittings and fasteners; pharmaceutical and food-processing equipment; chemical process piping and vessels; surgical implants; architectural cladding in coastal environments; cryogenic components. Carries a real cost premium over 304 (the added molybdenum is the expensive ingredient) — reserve 316 for chloride/marine/pharma environments where 304 would pit or corrode, rather than specifying it by default. Prefer 316L (low-carbon; see the 316L (DMLS) entry for the AM version) instead of standard 316 when the part will be welded or 3D-printed, since standard 316's carbon content raises the risk of post-weld corrosion.
